heard: A cosmic behemoth weighing three quadrillion suns is tearing itself apart. Many people imagine the universe's heaviest distant galaxy cluster is a single, peaceful object. In 2012, astronomers analyzed an extreme giant nicknamed El Gordo, Spanish for the fat one. This Titan in the Phoenix constellation produces the most x-rays of any known distant cluster. But data reveals El Gordo is actually two separate subclusters, colliding at millions of kilometers per hour. The impact is so violent that hot gas was wrenched away from unseen dark matter. It's massive weight warps spacetime, creating a magnifying glass that bends light from background galaxies. Instead of a single giant, we find that the heaviest distant clusters are actually catastrophic collisions.
differences: 'its' heard as 'it is' after 'unseen dark matter'
